Strategy.Name: Bad History Data Check [Rev. A]
Strategy.Description:
Bad History Data Check - Rev A. 

Note! Requires the Community Components Library Version 2010.11 (minimum)

Use this Strategy to check your historical data for problems.  The Strategy writes its report to the "Debug window".  View the Debug window by selecting it from the "Tools" menu.  The Strategy looks for the following problems in your data:

  1. Bars that fall on Saturdays or Sundays

  2. Duplicate dates

  3. Bars where the open or close is less than the low or greater than the high

  4. Out of sequence dates

  5. Gaps of more than 3 days in the data

If you find any bad data, you can reload the data by right clicking on a chart and selecting "Reload Chart History" from the popup menu.

Rev A. Enhancements / Additions

Rev A. eliminates virtually all false alarms for gap bars, and, gaps that are reported indicate the number of market days that are missing not including weekends or holidays.  Holidays, however, must be entered in the Markets.xml file found in the ..\1.0.0.0\Data folder.  This file contains U.S. Market holidays back to 2004 and is installed with Wealth-Lab.  You can beef up the holiday section to eliminate false alarms prior to 2004.  Holidays are taken from the primary Bars object and assumed to be the same holidays for all symbols in the DataSet.

There are also three "switches" to control the mode of operation and debug output:

  1. Full DataSet: Select "0" for testing only one symbol.  Select "1" to check the entire DataSet.  
    Note! When testing the entire DataSet: a) click on one symbol only, and b) make sure the chart is not in Streaming mode. 

  2. Show Only Errors: "0" will show all symbols, even if the data are "OK!".  Select "1" to see only symbols that have errors in the debug output. 
    The latter is useful with the Full DataSet option so that you can quickly identify only the symbols with errors.

  3. Check 4pm: Default "0".  Select "1" to check that the last bar of intraday history is 4pm (or 1pm on short days).  Generally, it's most likely that symbol will trade in the last interval of the day, so this can be used to detect a truncated intraday history. This selection applies only to intraday data checks.

Important!
Finally, at the end of the data check and if applicable for the DataSet's Static Provider, the script asks if you want to delete the data files with bad bars from the Provider's DataStore. This option is most useful when a DataSet returns dozens of symbols with errors.  In this case, look at the debug window to determine if you want to delete all the bad data files.  If so, click "Yes" to allow the script to delete the files, and once complete use the Data Manager to update the DataSet, which will "reload" the deleted symbol histories.  Note that following a reload errors may still be detected, and in this baseline case you should generally choose not to delete files.
